explain.what: Monthly count of US jobs added outside farming, from the BLS employment report (first Friday, 08:30 ET).
explain.why: The single biggest scheduled mover of index futures: it sets the tone for growth and Fed policy at once. Big beats or misses produce violent 08:30 moves and often the day's range.

explain.what: Personal-consumption-expenditures price index ex food and energy.
explain.why: The Fed's official inflation target measure; usually well forecast from CPI/PPI, so surprises are rare but potent.

explain.what: Gross domestic product growth, quarterly, annualised.
explain.why: Backward-looking, so the market reacts to revisions and the price deflator more than the headline.

explain.what: A scheduled speech or remarks by a Fed official.
explain.why: Usually minor, but voters signalling a change of view can move rate expectations mid-session.

explain.what: The Fed's policy-rate decision and statement (14:00 ET), followed by the Chair's press conference (14:30).
explain.why: The highest-impact scheduled event; the window before and after is prone to whipsaws. Dot plot / projections on quarterly meetings.

explain.what: Weekly count of new unemployment-benefit filings (Thursdays 08:30 ET).
explain.why: The most timely labour-market read; usually a small mover unless it jumps, which flags a turn in the cycle.

explain.why: The highest-impact scheduled event; the window before and after is prone to whipsaws. Dot plot / projections on quarterly meetings.

explain.what: Purchasing managers' survey of factories; 50 separates expansion from contraction (10:00 ET).
explain.why: A 10:00 ET print inside the window; the prices-paid and employment sub-indices are read for inflation and jobs.
